title: Improve SRD gameplay-readiness reporting
description:
Improve gameplay-readiness report accuracy for partially structured records.

Problem:
The ngcj gameplay-readiness report is useful, but it appears to undercount some existing structure. It marks all 15 conditions as prose-only even though records such as Blinded have effects and Exhaustion has structured levels.

Why this matters:
The report is becoming an important work-ordering signal. If it overstates prose-only gaps, it can mislead planning and obscure real progress.

Scope:
- Review gameplay-readiness report classification logic.
- Count existing structure for conditions, features, actions, equipment, magic items, and other record kinds consistently.
- Distinguish "prose-only", "partially structured", and "deterministically executable" where possible.
- Keep conservative warnings, but avoid false prose-only classifications.
- Add focused tests/fixtures for records with partial structure.

Acceptance criteria:
- Blinded and Exhaustion are not reported as fully prose-only when structured data exists.
- The report clearly distinguishes prose-only from partially structured records.
- The report remains conservative about deterministic executability.
- Existing gameplay-readiness findings remain actionable and not noisy.
- npm run typecheck passes.
- npm test passes.
- npm run check passes.
- npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack passes and regenerated pack output is intentional.
close_reason: Completed in branch eshyra-vk23-rest: gameplay-readiness partial-structure reporting, clean Biome 2.5.1 check output, and SRD option source-page attribution.
